definition.explanation:
Azure Backup can assign daily, weekly, monthly, and yearly retention to the same recovery point when that point matches the configured rule, and the point is preserved according to the longest matching retention. Here, backups occur daily at 11:00 PM. Weekly retention applies to Sunday backups for 10 weeks, monthly retention applies to backups taken on day 1 of the month for 36 months, and yearly retention applies to backups taken on March 1 for 10 years. Therefore, the Sunday, March 1 backup is a yearly retention point and is kept for 10 years. The Sunday, November 1 backup is not a yearly point, but it is both a weekly and monthly point; the monthly retention of 36 months is longer, so that point is kept for 36 months.

You have an Azure subscription that includes resources in the East US and West US Azure regions. Each region contains a virtual network, and the virtual networks are peered.

definition.explanation:
Azure Virtual WAN is the Azure service intended for connecting branch offices and on-premises datacenters to Azure through regional virtual hubs. An administrator creates a custom role that has an assignable scope set to a resource group named **RG1** in **Sub1**.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Select the custom role and add Sub1 and Sub2 to the assignable scopes. Remove RG1 from the assignable scopes.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Create a new custom role for Sub1. Create a new custom role for Sub2. Remove the role from RG1.

Modifying the grant control of the existing policy, which already scopes to the Global Administrators group and to sign-ins from untrusted locations, is exactly where the MFA requirement and the device-join requirement are added together, so this action satisfies the stated goal.

Likewise, the multifactor authentication user-settings page only manages a user's registered authentication methods; it does not configure Conditional Access conditions such as untrusted locations or grant requirements such as device join. definition.answerText:
On the **Device settings** page (Microsoft Entra ID / Azure AD > Devices > All devices > Device settings), change two settings:

1. **Users may join devices to Azure AD** (now labeled *Users might join devices to Microsoft Entra ID*): set to **Selected**, and add the **Pilot** group in the selected users list. This restricts device join to only members of the Pilot group.
2. **Require Multi-Factor Auth to join devices**: set to **Yes**. This forces users to complete a second factor (e.g., a mobile phone prompt/code) before they can join a device to Azure AD/Microsoft Entra ID.

All other settings on the page (local administrators, device registration/"Users may register their devices", Enterprise State Roaming, MDM/MAM URLs) are left unchanged.

choices.text: Create an incoming security rule for port 443 from the Internet. Associate the NSG to the subnet that contains the web servers.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Create an outgoing security rule for port 443 from the Internet. Associate the NSG to the subnet that contains the web servers.

choices.text: Create an incoming security rule for port 443 from the Internet. Associate the NSG to all the subnets.

definition.explanation: To allow users to reach App1 over HTTPS, the network security group must permit **inbound** traffic from the Internet on TCP port 443 to the subnet or NIC hosting the web servers.
